div.head: Ine 6.5
div.ab: Gif ðonne on gebeorscipe hie geciden, ⁊ oðer hiora mid geðylde hit forbere, geselle se oðer XXX scill. to wite.
. . . onne bið on gebeo . . ., ⁊ o . . . ðylde . ., . . . se oðer . . .
Gif ðonne on gebeorscipe hi geciden, ⁊ oþer heora mid geðylde hit forbere, gesylle se oþer XXX scll' to wite.
Gyf ðonne on gebeorscipe hi geciden, ⁊ oðer heora mid geþyldé hít forbere, gesylle se oðer XXX scill' to wite.
Si quilibet in potatione decertent, et alter eorum cum patientia sustineat, reddat alius XXX sol. wite (forisfacti).
Gif ðonne on gebeorscipe hie geciden, ⁊ oðer hiora mid geðylde hit forbere, geselle se oðer XXX scill. to wite.
Gif ðonne on gebeorscipe hie geciden, ⁊ oðer hiora mid geðylde hit forbere, geselle se oþer xxx sciƚƚ to wite.
Wenn sie [beide] jedoch beim Biergelage zanken, und der eine von ihnen es mit Geduld erträgt, so gebe der andere [dem König] 30 Schill. zur Strafe.
If, however, they [two] quarrel at a beer-feast, and one of them bears it with patience, let the other give [the king] 30 shillings as a fine.
If, however, two men quarrel over their cups and one endures it patiently, the other [who has recourse to violence] shall pay a fine of 30 shillings.
If, however, they quarrel at their drinking, and one of them bears it with patience, the other is to pay 30 shillings as a fine.
If, however, they quarrel at drinking, and one person bears it with patience, let the other [who resorted to violence] pay 30 shillings as fine.

note.label: compare
note.quote: geciden means to have a verbal altercation. Compare Hloþhere and Eadric §7 [L11].

note.label: cf.
note.quote: Note that §6.5 set a fine of 30 shillings for an altercation in words rather than blows

added later after wite, and referred to this place by a mark

Vgl. Gl Biergelage 7d. Da cidan nur ‘schelten, streiten in Worten’ bedeutet, ist auch hier wohl nicht Bluttat gemeint, sondern eine dazu vorbereitende Handlung. — Die 30 Schill. stehen den 12 Kentischen gleich, die Hl 13 für Verletzung des Biergelagefriedens fordert: vielleicht Ines Quelle; s. o. Einl. 11

Cf. Gl Biergelage 7d. Since cidan means only ‘to scold, quarrel in words’, here too probably no act of bloodshed is meant, but an action leading up to one. — The 30 shill. are equivalent to the 12 Kentish shill. that Hl 13 demands for breach of the peace of the drinking-bout: perhaps Ine’s source; see above Introduction 11
